Headline: Royal Conservatory
Text: Received the highest mark in Saskatchewan for Royal Conservatory of Music Examination "First Class Honours with Distinction” Regional Gold Medals are awarded for each academic year (i.e., September 1 to August 31) in each province or designated region to the candidates in Levels 1 to 10, plus Elementary and Intermediate Pedagogy, who have obtained the highest marks in each level and in each of the following disciplines: accordion, brass/woodwinds, guitar, harp, organ, percussion, piano, speech arts and drama, strings and voice. To qualify for Regional Gold Medals, candidates must have obtained at least 80 percent in the practical examination and have completed the co-requisite theory examinations for their respective level.

Headline: AcTal
Text: A classroom of 30 kids from various elementary schools were pooled together at Greystone Heights Elementary School where they took part in 4 years of an accelerated learning environment. The Grade 4 teacher completes a referral form that is intended to provide a multitude of information (i.e.: indicators of a student's cognitive abilities, academic achievement, performance in a variety of settings, interests, creativity, motivation, learning characteristics and behavior) from a variety of sources (i.e.: test scores, school grades, comments by teachers and parents). All of the data provided for each student are reviewed by the admissions committee using a selection criteria rubric. A maximum of 28 students are chosen for the Grade five class.

Headline: Advanced Program
Text: I was one of 60 Highschool Students who were accepted each academic year into the Advanced Program. This regimen was designed to prepare the students for excellent in post-secondary education by emphasizing the analaysis of learning itself, knowledge and existentialism, critical thinking, and long term independent research projects that were unique in comparison to the standard provincial highschool curriculum. "Walter Murray houses Saskatoon Public Schools' designated program for gifted students in Grades 9 to 12. The Advanced Program is for students who have high ability, an excellent academic record and a strong work ethic. The program is based on the integration of concepts across subject areas and the development of skills such as critical and creative thinking, communication and presentation, synthesis and analysis. This integration and interdisciplinary approach allows Advanced Program students to master subject content."

Headline: Michael Smith Science Challence
Text: Recipient of the University of British Columbia Certificate of Excellence - winner of the Michael Smith Science Challenge and ranked in the top 3% of science and physics student competitors in Canada – Presented by the Faculty of Science. The Michael Smith Science Challenge is a national competition written by students in Grade 10 Science or lower. It emphasizes logical thinking, and covers material in the science curriculum common to all provinces. It is named in honour of UBC’s Nobel Prize Winner Dr. Michael Smith, and is sponsored by the UBC faculty of Science and NSERC PromoScience. Prizes are awarded to the top students (and their teachers) in each province and nationally.
